subject.title: Feature: Global session reset on auth switch

question: For an all-session auth refresh, should active runs finish with their captured credentials or be cancelled for an immediate cutover, and should explicit user-selected per-session auth overrides be preserved?
rationale: Current source establishes the missing global surface and an operator-admin precedent, but in-flight credential use and user-override semantics are security and product-policy choices that automation cannot safely select.

options.title: Graceful refresh, preserve overrides
options.body: Use `operator.admin`, clear automatic auth pins and backend bindings for subsequent runs, allow already-admitted runs to finish, and preserve explicit user-selected profile overrides.

options.title: Immediate refresh, preserve overrides
options.body: Cancel active runs before clearing automatic auth pins and backend bindings, while retaining explicit user-selected profile overrides.

options.title: Refresh every auth selection
options.body: Cancel or drain active runs and clear both automatic pins and explicit user overrides, making current global configuration authoritative for every session.

recommendation.title: Graceful refresh, preserve overrides
recommendation.body: Use `operator.admin`, clear automatic auth pins and backend bindings for subsequent runs, allow already-admitted runs to finish, and preserve explicit user-selected profile overrides.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history covers Gateway reset lifecycle ownership, administrative reset semantics, and the documented session auth-pinning contract.
